newsitem.title: UK: Lebed says Russia scaring off long term investors.
newsitem.headline: Lebed says Russia scaring off long term investors.

text.p: Former Russian security chief Alexander Lebed on Saturday called President Boris Yeltsin's government a "mutant creature" and said it had created a power vaccuum that was deterring long term investment.

Yeltsin's government had failed to create an effective mechanism of political power and without real authority there was no hope of economic growth, Lebed, president of the Russian People's Republican Party, told an investment conference.
"Long term investment is out of the question...What insane person would invest in a country where legislation changed all the time?" Lebed said.

Lebed, a former paratroop commander, was Boris Yeltsin's national security adviser until he was sacked last October after the president ruled against him in a bitter feud with Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov.

"The state authority is an administrative mutant, people are pressed from the top by the authorities and from below by crime and the thoughtless actions of the authorities have turned everyone in Russia into liars, crooks and thieves," Lebed said on Saturday.

He said Russia needed to do five things to solve the problem; transform the laws, create an effective system of law enforcement, make law abidance the norm, protect people from despotism and return people's trust.
He slated the government for non-payment of wages and pensions in order to curb inflation and said no other government would have got away with it.
"There is apathy in the country," he said. "We need to recreate the opportunity for people to work honestly, to revive factories and create new jobs," he said.
"The most important priority of Russia is to put in place a middle class," Lebed said.
He said he would like to see the creation of a "civilised" stock market, to overcome the fears of long term investors.
Any uncontrolled monopoly harmed the economy and should be regulated, Lebed said but he opposed the break-up of powerful giants like Gazprom.
The state should help form financial and industrial groups that could compete on the international arena.
"I am not just for a mixed economy, but for the multi-level economy," he said.
Lebed also said he was looking into creating a forum of politicians and business leaders to help guide Russia into the 21st Century.
